players.product: Turnkey HPC data-center campuses leased to hyperscalers (Barber Lake, Black Pearl, Stingray - Texas) - ex-Bitcoin-mining, now 'Cipher Digital'

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: to date Cipher has executed two data center campus leases (Barber Lake, Black Pearl) representing 600 megawatts of gross capacity and approximately $9,300,000,000 in contracted revenue, with initial terms of ten to fifteen years and multiple extension options; based solely on executed contracts, the leases are expected to generate $669,000,000 average annualized net operating income from October 2026 to September 2036, with approximately $754,000,000 of annual NOI projected by 2035. Rent payments on the initial leases begin this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 600 megawatts of gross capacity; approximately $9,300,000,000 in contracted revenue; $669,000,000 average annualized NOI; approximately $754,000,000 annual NOI by 2035

capex.metric: contracted lease revenue (two leases, 600 MW gross)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: fourth-quarter revenue was $60,000,000, down from Q3 on the difficult Bitcoin mining environment and Bitcoin price decline; mining revenue is expected to decrease further as Black Pearl miners are decommissioned. GAAP net loss of $734,000,000, driven largely by a $450,000,000 noncash mark-to-market on the embedded derivative of the 2031 convertible notes, plus a $90,000,000 write-down on Black Pearl miners and a $45,000,000 Odessa PP&E impairment.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $60,000,000; GAAP net loss $734,000,000 (incl. $450,000,000 noncash derivative mark-to-market)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on project financing: in November Cipher raised $1,400,000,000 of five-year senior secured notes at 7.125% for Barber Lake, then a $333,000,000 tack-on after the lease upsizing, bringing Barber Lake debt financing to $1,730,000,000 (plus $477,000,000 of additional equity); this month it raised $2,000,000,000 of five-year senior secured notes at 6.125% for Black Pearl, oversubscribed 6.5 times with approximately $13,000,000,000 in orders, including a $233,000,000 capex reimbursement. Both projects are fully funded through substantial completion and management does not anticipate needing additional equity for currently contracted developments. Year-end unrestricted liquidity was $754,000,000 ($628,000,000 cash and $125,000,000 Bitcoin).
quarterly_data.figure: $1,730,000,000 Barber Lake debt at 7.125%; $2,000,000,000 Black Pearl notes at 6.125%; $754,000,000 unrestricted liquidity

quarterly_data.signal: Stingray (Andrews, Texas): fully interconnection approved for 100 megawatts and on track to energize in the fourth quarter of this year, with substation development underway; CEO says Cipher has identified a preferred partner and is in advanced lease negotiations, expects the lease economics to be among the most favorable it has achieved, and is exploring behind-the-meter solutions to expand capacity over time.
quarterly_data.figure: 100 megawatts; energization in the fourth quarter of this year

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline: roughly 3.4 gigawatt development pipeline, all prioritized for HPC. Cipher acquired Ulysses, a 200 megawatt site in Ohio with PJM interconnection approvals, expected to energize in 2027, with multiple hyperscalers in data rooms doing diligence. Reveille is approved for 70 megawatts (energize 2027); CEO says it is a little small for most hyperscalers and more interesting to neoclouds, with credit wrappers or prepayments among the options discussed. Stingray, Reveille and Ulysses are the 370 megawatts currently being marketed; McLean, McKeska and Colchis are in earlier discussions with hyperscaler interest while awaiting final ERCOT interconnection approval (ERCOT's existing development and stakeholder process for a potential batch study is expected to last until June 2026). CEO: demand for power-dense hyperscale infrastructure continues to outpace supply, and it remains a very favorable environment to negotiate economics.
quarterly_data.figure: 3.4 gigawatt pipeline; 370 megawatts currently marketed (Stingray 100 megawatts, Reveille 70 megawatts, Ulysses 200 megawatts)

quarterly_data.signal: Exit from Bitcoin mining: Cipher sold its 49% interests in three 40 megawatt joint venture sites (Alborz, Bear and Chief) to Canaan in an all-stock transaction; all Black Pearl mining rigs have been sold, marked for sale or redeployed to Odessa, leaving a hash rate of approximately 11.6 exahash per second. Odessa runs 207 megawatts under a fixed-price PPA with Luminant at approximately $0.028 per kilowatt hour expiring July 2027; CEO says multiple tenants are interested in an HPC site there, a conversion would require recutting the PPA and ground lease with Luminant, and July 2027 is the outside date. Cipher held approximately 1,166 Bitcoin as of February 20 and expects to exit the position, likely by 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 207 megawatts; approximately 11.6 exahash per second; approximately $0.028 per kilowatt hour PPA to July 2027; approximately 1,166 Bitcoin

quarterly_data.signal: Behind-the-meter power: CEO says he has not seen any decrease in hyperscaler interest in Texas despite the ERCOT changes; all of the hyperscalers are also looking at behind-the-meter solutions as a way to faster power, and Cipher has some of its best resources investigating co-located generation using its access to natural gas pipeline capacity at sites like Stingray and Barber Lake, which he expects to become a major part of the portfolio over time (no timeline given).

Tenant strategy: CEO says Cipher is talking to all the other hyperscalers and pretty much all the neoclouds, as well as equipment manufacturers interested in neocloud success; early leases prioritized counterparty credit quality to debt-finance the builds, and repeat work with existing tenants brings efficiencies from similar design philosophies. Target model: find a couple of new sites, sign a couple of new leases and build a couple of new data centers per year, with the team being deepened so it could build four data centers at once.

connects_to.relationship: Barber Lake (TX) AI/HPC data-center development for Fluidstack/Google

contracts.signal: CFO: during the fourth quarter Cipher upsized its Barber Lake lease with Fluidstack supported by Google, at improved economic terms. CEO: construction is well underway (concrete foundations poured, structural steel going vertical, MEP work commenced); approximately 95% of long lead equipment and 100% of the necessary workforce are secured, over 400 personnel are on-site each workday, and the project is tracking to meet early access and substantial completion milestones.
contracts.units: approximately 95% of long lead equipment secured; over 400 personnel on-site

connects_to.relationship: Black Pearl (TX) AI/HPC data-center campus lease to Amazon Web Services

contracts.signal: CFO: during the fourth quarter Cipher executed a long-term lease agreement with AWS; CEO describes it as a triple-net lease at Black Pearl, with engineering, procurement and construction underway, Bitcoin mining decommissioning completed this week, and approximately 85% of the infrastructure currently deployed expected to be repurposed for the AWS lease. The $2,000,000,000 bond fully funds Black Pearl through substantial completion.
